title: Lead 4: chore-type priority ordering (weeds vs harvest tier order in _build_sweep)
verdict_explanation: Original 4-test external-opponent design showed a promising positive-signed result (pooled t=1.97, n=160), but a scaled, more direct head-to-head confirmation test (mini_engine.evaluate(), 200 games, seed-matched, both seats) reversed direction: batch 1 (n=100) t=-2.34 (significantly negative), full sample (n=200) t=-1.53 (not significant, negative-leaning). The effect does not replicate at scale under the more rigorous design. Closed as FAILED_CONFIRMATION, not promoted, not worth further causal testing.
decision_point: candidates/V3_15.py:724 _build_sweep(), tier order constant, currently ['urgent','harvest','weeds','water'] (or with fert: ['urgent','fert','harvest','weeds','water'])

variant.change: weeds moved immediately after urgent/fert, ahead of harvest. Two-line change, otherwise byte-identical to candidates/V3_15.py.

rng_side_effect_audit: Tier-order change only affects same-day task sequencing within _build_sweep; does not touch _spawn_weeds or shop-unlock RNG streams by code inspection. Full trace-level audit not run this round.
recommendation: None. Closed as FAILED_CONFIRMATION. Not worth a causal-intervention step since the effect did not survive scaled statistical confirmation.

scaled_confirmation.method: mini_engine.evaluate() direct head-to-head, variant vs baseline, seed-matched both-seats
